solutions.title: Jump six steps at a time
solutions.explanation:
Substituting the recurrence into itself cancels terms and lets us move back several indices at once. For \(n\ge 4\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(n)&=[f(n-2)-f(n-3)+(n-1)]-f(n-2)+n\\
&=-f(n-3)+2n-1.
\end{aligned}
\]
For \(n\ge 7\), we can apply this same identity to \(f(n-3)\), obtaining
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(n)&=-[-f(n-6)+2(n-3)-1]+2n-1\\
&=f(n-6)+6.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus decreasing the input by \(6\) decreases the function value by \(6\). Since \(2018=2+336\cdot6\), repeated use of this identity gives
\[
f(2018)=f(2)+336\cdot6=1+2016=\boxed{2017}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{B}\).
